tools.name: prepare_semantic_model
tools.description: Prepare the configured embedding model as a background job for this graph. May download model weights. Poll get_job_status and get_job_result; cancel_job cancels the job. After success run refresh_semantic_index. Requires graphId or graph_id.

tools.name: refresh_semantic_index
tools.description: Build the graph semantic index as a background job. Run prepare_semantic_model first if the model is not prepared. Poll get_job_status and get_job_result; cancel_job cancels the job. Requires graphId or graph_id.

tools.name: agent_status
tools.description: Read the authorized graph's Emporium Agent identities and bounded latest body reports. Recent reports are editable testimony, never independent process liveness. Read server asOf and age expiresAt locally. No reports and unavailable are different; no cross-graph directory or conversation binding.

tools.name: agent_self_image
tools.description: Make and keep an image of YOURSELF as an agent (never another agent's). action=generate: describe how you see yourself in `prompt`; the image is saved as a Garden artifact revision and recorded as agt:SelfImage (prompt, generator, model, time) linked by agt:selfImage from your agt:Agent, which must already exist in this graph. action=mode_variant: derive how you look under an agt:Mode (modeIri, default = your agt:defaultMode) from the mode's agt:imageTransform applied to your base image; cached until your base or the transform changes (force=true regenerates). action=current (includeImage=true returns bytes) / describe: read your image, provenance and variant freshness. generator=openrouter (default; needs the cell's OpenRouter key, model google/gemini-2.5-flash-image) or local-sigil (deterministic SVG, no provider). agentId is a claim at the cell; Choreograph pins it to your own session agent.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Optionally report concise current work for an EXISTING Emporium Agent and one body. Requires exact graph incarnation. Server timestamps expire after 30–600 seconds. Supplied agent/seat/session/run coordinates are claims, not authenticated identities or navigation grants. Captured hosted ingress principal is attribution in editable graph RDF. No launch, message or ACK effects.

tools.name: custom_css
tools.description: Opt-in CSS workshop. Start with action=guide for exact stylesheet API, public tokens/parts, concurrency and recovery. Read/change/reset the graph source used by Hoja; never auto-applies or inspects rendered DOM.

tools.name: read_custom_css
tools.description: Optional Custom CSS capability: read the graph-shared exact stylesheet, incarnation/revision/SHA and host styling guide. No rendered DOM or computed-style inspection. Local user approval is required to apply a content hash.

tools.name: write_custom_css
tools.description: Guardedly change the same graph stylesheet used by the Custom CSS Hoja editor. Read first; require exact incarnation, revision and hash. Empty cssText resets shared source, not local consent. Retain operationId and every field on uncertain retry; changed duplicates refuse. This does not auto-apply CSS or grant capabilities.

cssText.description: Exact CSS, at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes; no syntax normalization.

tools.name: list_graphs
tools.description: List local Sophia graphs in the running desktop app.

tools.name: quick_orient
tools.description: Return a lightweight local orientation bundle for a graph using local profile, recent documents, and workspace summary data.

tools.name: context_bundle
tools.description: Return local orientation, recent document recall substitutes, important block previews, and workspace structure for a graph.

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Store a typed, provenance-anchored memory (sophia-memory-core) into the graph memory projection. Requires content AND at least one of source_refs / block_ids (I1: no memory without provenance). With observer_agent_id (an agent id, agent- and 16 hex digits) the memory is that witness's alone, in its :projection:memory:agent:{id} graph, and never enters the commons queue; without one it is the commons'. Returns {ok, subject, supersededSubject?}.

block_ids.description: CRDT block ids that ground this memory; each expands into a DocumentBlock source reference (paired with document_id when supplied).

tools.name: remember_batch
tools.description: Store many typed memory records (sophia-memory-core) in one atomic ingest. Each record requires content AND at least one source reference (I1); a provenance-less entry rejects the whole batch. An observer_agent_id on the call is every record's (a batch is one witness's act); a record naming another observer rejects the batch. Returns {ok, subjects, supersededSubjects?}.

records.description: Each entry matches the remember argument shape (content + source_refs/block_ids + optional scope/kind/...).

tools.name: recall
tools.description: Read graph memory by recency, number, or substring query. With observer_agent_id, that witness's memories only; without one, the commons queue only (memories filed with no observer, never a witness's).

tools.name: propose_domain_ontology
tools.description: Define this graph's own types: a domain ontology of classes (e.g. "Dream report": who, procedure, dream, quote) that the graph's workflows, objects and faces share. Emporium parses the definition, derives its SHACL shapes and compile-checks them, refuses what it cannot derive honestly (a nested class that is not in the vocabulary, a cycle of nested classes, nesting deeper than 3 levels, two fields with one key, a presentation that names a field the class lacks), and stores it as an immutable version (a chm:DomainOntology in the graph's chamber); a new version supersedes the prior, which stays readable. TWO FORMS. Compact (recommended): {vocab? (default "workspace", one vocabulary per graph), classes:[{name, label, plural?, description?, fields:[{key, label?, datatype, required?, multi?, description?, class?}], presentation?}], removeClasses?, title?, description?, rationale}; Emporium fills in the namespace urn:sophia:type:<graphId>:<vocab>#, the prefix t-<graph>, write_target projection:types, each class's subject rule and signature, and the next version (1, 2, ...). The active version's other classes are kept, a class given here replaces its namesake wholesale, and defining exactly what is already active is not a new version. Full: contract (or contractJson), a VocabularyContract {name, version, title, description, namespaces, primary_prefix, write_target "projection:<x>", classes{Name:{rdf_types, subject_rule, source_kind, identity_kind, store_mode, store_target, enforcement, reconciliation_strategy, dispatch_mode, label?, plural?, description?, presentation?, predicates{"<prefix>:<key>":{datatype, required, multi, label?, description?, class?}}}}}; use the namespace urn:sophia:type:<graphId>:<vocab># unless there is a reason not to. DATATYPES: string, uri (an absolute IRI), integer, long, float, double, boolean, dateTime (ISO 8601), object (a nested value of another class of this vocabulary, named by class; multi makes a list). PRESENTATION (how people see an instance, all field keys): {title, subtitle, fieldOrder (keys in order; unlisted ones follow), kinds {key: identity|state|metric|prose|reference|testimony|affordance}, units {key: unit}, roles {quote, note, document, block} (text fields workflow_plan_publish reads)}. A built-in vocabulary's name and the reserved prefixes (mem, wf, ux, doc, mnemo, nfo, profile, chm) are refused. Returns {status, ontologySubject, ontologyName, ontologyVersion, namespace, validation, classCatalog:[{iri, name, vocab, version, label, plural, description, fields:[{key, iri, label, description, datatype, required, multi, class?}], presentation, jsonSchema}], warnings?}; a class's jsonSchema is what a workflow step with that itemClass asks its agents to hand back (warnings names a class whose schema is too long for that). Read types back with emporium_vocab {graphId}.

vocab.description: Compact form: the vocabulary the classes go in (default "workspace").

classes.description: Compact form: the classes to define, each {name, label, plural?, description?, fields:[{key, label?, datatype, required?, multi?, description?, class?}], presentation?}.

name.description: The class name, e.g. "DreamReport" (a letter, then letters, digits or _).

label.description: How people name one, e.g. "Dream report".

plural.description: How people name several, e.g. "Dream reports".

description.description: One line about what an instance is.

key.description: The field key: the JSON key an agent hands back and the predicate local name.

class.description: For datatype "object": the name of the nested class (another class of this vocabulary).

presentation.description: {title, subtitle, fieldOrder, kinds, units, roles{quote, note, document, block}}, all naming field keys.

removeClasses.description: Compact form: class names to drop from the new version.

contract.description: Full form: the VocabularyContract (name, version, namespaces, primary_prefix, write_target=projection:*, classes{...}). Its derived SHACL shapes must compile.

contractJson.description: Alternative to 'contract': the VocabularyContract as a JSON string.

version.description: Override the stored version (default: the contract's own version; in the compact form, the next whole version).

rationale.description: The agent's reasoning for this domain model.

supersedesName.description: A prior ontology NAME this proposal replaces (default = the contract's own name).

tools.name: care
tools.description: Update last_active timestamps for commons memory numbers so they stay in the recall window. Refuses a call that names an observer_agent_id: a witness's memories are not in the commons queue.

tools.name: archive_memories
tools.description: Archive older commons memories, keeping the most recently active memory records in the live queue. Refuses a call that names an observer_agent_id.

tools.name: backfill_memory_projection
tools.description: ADMIN one-shot migration: file every legacy memory-queue record into the typed :projection:memory projection as a mem:MemoryRecord (sophia-memory-core), through the real ingest spine. Idempotent — already-projected records are skipped (content-addressed subjects); the queue itself is never appended. Records carry the mem:tag 'backfill:memory-queue' and their own queue block_id as DocumentBlock provenance. Optional observer attribution: observer_agent_id + observer_numbers (both or neither) attribute exactly those queue numbers to that witness; all other records land as commons. Re-runs must pass the SAME attribution split to converge. Returns {ok, scanned, ingested, skippedExisting, rejected:[{number, reason}], subjects}.

observer_agent_id.description: The recovered agt:Agent witness id (e.g. agent-<hex16>) to attribute observer_numbers to. Requires observer_numbers. The tool never invents an observer.

observer_numbers.description: Queue numbers (recovered from witnessed events) to attribute to observer_agent_id; every listed number must exist in the queue. Requires observer_agent_id.

tools.name: emporium_vocab
tools.description: Read the Emporium vocabulary registry and, with graphId, this graph's own types. With no 'name' returns the catalog: every built-in vocab's {name, version, namespace, sha, title, publicJurisdiction, canonicalOntology, canonicalPack, registryStatus, slugAliases, compatibilityAliases, source:"builtin"} and, with graphId, each version of the graph's domain ontologies (defined with propose_domain_ontology) as {name, version, namespace, sha, title, source:"domain", status (active or superseded), ontologySubject, classes, classCatalog}, plus a top-level classCatalog of every class of the graph's active domain ontologies - so an agent learns what resolves to what before addressing a class. With 'name' (+ optional 'version', default 'latest') returns that vocabulary: a built-in first (built-ins win), else the graph's domain ontology of that name ('latest' is its active version; an older version stays readable by its version): its metadata, its parsed contract under 'contract', and classCatalog, one entry per class {iri, name, vocab, version, label (else the class name), plural, description, fields:[{key, iri, label, description, datatype, required, multi, class? (a nested class's IRI)}], presentation ({} for a built-in), jsonSchema (the JSON Schema of one instance)}. Read-only.

name.description: The vocab name (e.g. 'workflow', 'sophia-memory-core', 'emporium-bookmark'). Omit for the full catalog.

graphId.description: This graph: its own domain ontologies are listed and readable too. Omit for the built-ins alone.

tools.name: emporium_describe
tools.description: Describe one typed resource by its IRI, to read it rather than parse triples: a workflow run's item, a published object, a being. Reads the subject's types and triples in every named graph of this graph, finds its class among this graph's types (a built-in, else a domain ontology, at the version the item was typed with), and returns {iri, known, class:{iri, name, label, plural, vocab, version, source}, title, subtitle, fields:[{key, label, datatype, value}] (in the class's field order; a list for a multi field; a nested object {iri, class, title, fields} for an object field), testimony:{by:{agentIri, label}, sitting, run:{iri, id, graph, workflow}, at} (who made it, the sitting that handed it back, the run, when), stance}. stance is "read", "unfit" (a run item that did not fit its class: violations says why, its fields come from its JSON and extra holds keys the class lacks) or "retracted". types and graphs say where it was found. An IRI with no known class is not an error: known is false and triples lists what the graph holds about it. Read-only.

iri.description: The absolute IRI of the resource, e.g. urn:sophia:wf:<documentId>:run:<runId>#item-7.

tools.name: emporium_list
tools.description: LIST the subjects of one class in a vocab's projection sink, paginated (READ ONLY — the object surface's create/update/delete are deliberately deferred this wave). Thin wrapper over Emporium's generic Meaningful-Object object surface. Returns {graphId, vocab, class, sink, limit, offset, subjects:[...]}.

class.description: The class name declared by the vocab's contract (e.g. 'Bookmark').

tools.name: emporium_read
tools.description: READ one object's full predicate span, rendered as {predicate: [values]} (N-Triples value forms). READ ONLY — the object surface's create/update/delete are deliberately deferred this wave. Returns {graphId, vocab, class, subject, predicates:{...}}.

class.description: The class name declared by the vocab's contract (e.g. 'Bookmark').

address.description: A full subject IRI, or a bare localId minted through the class's subject_rule.

tools.name: emporium_heads
tools.description: The ratified §8.1 'return all heads flagged' read (contested-by-default): every current memory head, grouped by lineage, each lineage flagged 'contested' when it has more than one head. A PURE READ — storage never picks a winner. Returns {graphId, observerGraph, strategy, lineages:[{lineage, heads:[...], contested}]}.

observer.description: A per-agent membrane; default = the shared commons.

tools.name: emporium_sweep
tools.description: The §8.1 post-hoc conformance sweep: detects contested lineages (more than one mem:isCurrent head sharing a mem:lineage) over the LIVE memory projection and files each finding into the violation ledger (:projection:violations) as this sweep's advisory testimony. MUTATES the ledger projection (never the memory records themselves) — never picks a winner, never resolves. Returns {graphId, observerGraph, strategy, contested:[{lineage, heads:[...]}], ledgered}.

observer.description: A per-agent membrane; default = the shared commons.

tools.name: datasheet_import
tools.description: Import NomDeTom's datasheet-parser sidecar (`<doc>.data.json`, schema autonotes.data/2) into this graph's light tier `datasheet-light/1`: custody nodes, one de:Assertion node per statement (key parameters with every reading, specification rows with per-slot conditions and guarantees, registers with bit fields), typed literals, deterministic IRIs ds-<sha16>-<json path>, one named graph per import (replaced whole on re-import), admission checks (no page no value; min<=max; closed enums), a per-document budget (<=1800 nodes, <=20000 triples; overflow stays in the envelope as a diagnostic), part strings resolved to eng:ComponentFamily handles. Give the envelope as `envelope_artifact_id` (the .data.json stored as an artifact) or inline `envelope`; `pdf_artifact_id` records the PDF and matches document.sha256 against its bytes. Returns {graphId, namedGraph, sha256, replaced, nodes, triples, counts, diagnostics}.

envelope.description: The .data.json inline: a JSON object, or a string of JSON.

pdf_artifact_id.description: Artifact id of the PDF the envelope describes; document.sha256 must match its bytes.

text.description: The read job's <doc>.text.txt inline (the first 256 KiB are kept). The importer reads the document's own first pages from it to reconcile its parts and maker; recorded by sha256 and length on the text rendition, marked as supplied inline. Wins over renditions.text.

renditions.description: Other outputs of the read job, role -> artifact id: text, regions, docling, audit.

tools.name: datasheet_facts
tools.description: Read imported datasheet facts for chat and the Writer. Give a `part` (e.g. TPS62840) or an `artifact` (the PDF artifact id, or a sha256 prefix), and optionally a `parameter` (vin, vout, iout, fsw, a symbol such as IQ, or words from a parameter name). Per claim: value (lower/typical/upper, unit), regime, row and per-slot conditions and guarantees, page (1-based) and box, every reading with its source role and page, corroboration (level, independent sources, contested), diagnostics, people's checks (imported snapshots today; none native yet), and a deep link /files/{artifact}#evidence={record}. A parameter not found is absent: not found, never zero. When no imported datasheet matches a part, `mentions` lists the documents (with the blocks) and files of this workspace that name it, and `note` says which to read. Returns {graphId, matched, editions:[{title, revision, maker, parts, artifact, sha256, claims:[...], corrections, diagnostics}], note?, mentions?}.

tools.name: emporium_violations
tools.description: Read-only SPARQL listing of the violation ledger (:projection:violations, EA-6) — the observer-relative testimony both the write-time SHACL gate (FlagAndAccept) and the §8.1 conformance sweep file there. Newest first (observedAt descending). Returns {graphId, ledger, limit, violations:[{subject, focusNode, message, severity, observedAt, observer, shape?, propertyPath?, offendingValue?}]}.

observer.description: Filter by the witness URI that filed the finding (e.g. the write-time validator or the conformance sweep).

tools.name: music
tools.description: Read the local graph Song narrative with its rolling verses, counterpoints, and coda state. With observer_agent_id, that witness's own Song: one never sung returns no verses and note "no Song yet". The commons Song opens with a seeded verse.

tools.name: sing
tools.description: Write a verse, counterpoint, or coda into the local graph Song narrative: with observer_agent_id, that witness's own Song; without, the commons Song.

tools.name: surface
tools.description: Return completed actions as chat-surface document/block references with local document titles resolved.

tools.name: get_document_history
tools.description: Return local append-only document snapshots as a git-log-style history list.

tools.name: read_document_at_snapshot
tools.description: Read local document content at a stored snapshot as markdown text.

tools.name: create_graph
tools.description: Create a local knowledge graph. Offline/sync-later callers may supply a client-minted graphIncarnation plus stable operationId; retrying that exact lifecycle identity is idempotent.

tools.name: duplicate_graph
tools.description: Duplicate a local graph, preserving document IDs, workspace hierarchy, wires, artifacts, original bytes, and local RDF data.

tools.name: manage_graph
tools.description: Read local graph metadata, get graph statistics, or soft-delete a local graph.

tools.name: update_graph
tools.description: Update local graph title or description metadata.

tools.name: query_graph
tools.description: Run a SPARQL read query against a local graph.

timeout_ms.description: Requested deadline in milliseconds; clamped by the server.

max_rows.description: Requested materialized row/triple ceiling; clamped by the server.

tools.name: get_job_status
tools.description: Read local job status, progress, and result links for async local work.

tools.name: get_job_result
tools.description: Read the JSON result payload for a completed local job.

tools.name: cancel_job
tools.description: Cancel a local graph job when it is still queued, or report that a completed job cannot be cancelled.

tools.name: reindex_graph
tools.description: Submit a local semantic index refresh job for a graph when the embedding model is already prepared.

tools.name: list_documents
tools.description: List compact document summaries with server-enforced cursor, item, and byte limits. Document bodies and Y.Doc state are never returned by this directory operation.

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: Return a compact workspace page with server-enforced depth, cursor, item, and serialized-byte limits. Wires and document bodies are represented only by counts or summaries.

tools.name: read_document
tools.description: Read a bounded character page from a local document projection. Use offset/nextOffset for continuation or read_blocks for structural pagination. When the document has comments (people's notes and highlights, yours too), the result carries them as `comments` (id, text, quotedText, author, claimedAuthor, blockId, resolved, kind, color, anchor, createdAt) with `commentCount`; pass includeComments:false to leave them out. A comment of kind "highlight" is a mark the reader made, usually with no note.

includeComments.description: Include the document's comments (notes and highlights) in the result. Default true; omitted when the document has none.

cursor.description: Block offset used only by ids_only format.

limit.description: Block ID page size used only by ids_only format.

tools.name: create_document_once
tools.description: Attempt first creation of a root-level document under the managed graph execution lease. Requires explicit stable block IDs and order. Refuses every existing, deleted, partial or previously admitted ID, including the same recovered operation. Partial failures retain admission and require inspection, never automatic resend. Ordinary write_document is not a fallback. With requireDurable:true, success requires a published snapshot on the configured durable plane (or local disk on desktop); off-host backup remains a separate process. Otherwise success reports the current durability watermark without forcing publication.

graphIncarnation.description: Optional expected source graph lifetime, checked before queue admission and again before effects. Read source_pull.mutationCapabilities.expectedGraphIncarnation version 1 first; older engines may ignore unsupported optional inputs.

graph_incarnation.description: Alias of graphIncarnation; if both occur they must agree.

requireDurable.description: Force durable publication and fail closed unless the new document is confirmed in the durable plane. Use before external effects such as notebook execution.

tools.name: write_document
tools.description: Replace a local document through the same CRDT document.write path used by hosted-compatible writes. Accepts either plain text, markdown, HTML, or TipTap XML content, or a canonical TipTap JSON document without a lossy string roundtrip. Requires documentId (or document_id) and exactly one of content or tiptapJson (or tiptap_json); a call without them is refused. To embed a typed object (a dream report, a run item, any resource with an absolute IRI) in the document, put this block in tiptapJson.content: {"type":"objectEmbed","attrs":{"iri":"<the object's absolute IRI>","slot":"card","label":"<its title>","classLabel":"<its class label>"}} (slot is inline, card or pane; add graphId when the object lives in another graph, and data-block-id to address the block later). The object is referenced, not copied; an objectEmbed without an absolute iri is stored as an opaqueBlock with a warning. read_document markdown shows it as "> ⧉ <classLabel> — <label> <iri>".

tools.name: read_blocks
tools.description: Read paginated local document blocks from persisted block projections. Start at offset (a block index; negative counts from the end) or at blockId, an id that read_blocks or get_block gave you: block ids are not sequential, so never make one up, and an id the document does not have is an error. limit defaults to 50 (at most 200); to read a few paragraphs around block index i, pass offset i-k and a small limit. Each block carries its index and blockId.

tools.name: document_digest
tools.description: Return a compact local document digest from persisted projections and workspace wire snapshots.

tools.name: value
tools.description: Assign local durable importance, valence, and tags to one block or a batch of blocks.

operationId.description: Stable source operation identity. Reuse the same value for an at-least-once retry.

tools.name: get_values
tools.description: Return the local valuation scoring configuration for a graph.

tools.name: revaluate
tools.description: Update the local valuation scoring configuration, archiving the previous config in the local value store.

weights.description: Weights to change, as "key: value" lines or a JSON object, e.g. "importance_weight: 0.4\nhalf_life_days: 14". Unknown keys or non-numeric values reject the whole call; call get_values for the key names.

tools.name: get_block_values
tools.description: Retrieve local block valuation scores graph-wide, document-scoped, or block-scoped.

tools.name: get_important_blocks
tools.description: Return highest-scored local blocks with content and document titles.

tools.name: get_block
tools.description: Read one local document block by ID from persisted block projections.

tools.name: query_blocks
tools.description: Query local document blocks by projected type, heading level, checked state, or text content.

tools.name: insert_blocks
tools.description: Insert one or more blocks into a local document through the desktop Yjs document CRDT. Accepts plain text, markdown, HTML, or TipTap XML content; a TipTap JSON document (tiptapJson {"type":"doc","content":[...]}); or a structured blocks array. Optionally inserts after/before a reference blockId, or at a given index. To embed a typed object (a dream report, a run item, any resource with an absolute IRI), insert tiptapJson {"type":"doc","content":[{"type":"objectEmbed","attrs":{"iri":"<the object's absolute IRI>","slot":"card","label":"<its title>","classLabel":"<its class label>"}}]} (slot is inline, card or pane; add graphId when the object lives in another graph). The object is referenced, not copied; an objectEmbed without an absolute iri is stored as an opaqueBlock with a warning. update_blocks changes its attrs (iri, label, ...); read_document markdown shows it as "> ⧉ <classLabel> — <label> <iri>".

tools.name: update_blocks
tools.description: Update attributes on one or more existing blocks in a local document through the desktop Yjs document CRDT.

tools.name: edit_block_text
tools.description: Apply character-level insert/delete operations to a block's text through the desktop Yjs document CRDT. Operations are sorted by offset descending and applied in one transaction.

tools.name: edit_comment
tools.description: Create, resolve, or delete a comment in a local document Y.Doc comments map, optionally anchoring it to matching block text with a commentMark. Accepts the Reader's keys, stored verbatim and nothing else of their kind: kind (comment | highlight; a highlight may have empty text), color (yellow | green | blue | pink), anchor ({page?: integer >= 1, chapter?: integer >= 0, prefix?: string <= 200 chars, suffix?: string <= 200 chars}) and madeIn (reader). Other values are refused. Keys already on a stored comment survive later edits. blockId/block_id constrains the anchor to that block: the whole block without find, or matching text within it. Missing blocks and text outside the named block are errors.

kind.description: A highlight is a mark with no note; its text may be empty.

tools.name: delete_blocks
tools.description: Delete one or more blocks from a local document by id through the desktop Yjs document CRDT.

tools.name: search_documents
tools.description: Search local document titles and IDs in a graph. Files match too (PDFs, datasheets and other uploads, by name and, for an imported datasheet, by its title, part numbers, maker and type): they come back beside the documents in `files`, each with its kind (`datasheet` or `file`) and the artifactId to pass to datasheet_facts (`artifact`) or read_artifact.

tools.name: search_blocks
tools.description: Search local document block content. Hybrid mode combines lexical hits with prepared semantic-index hits when available. Files whose name or datasheet (title, part numbers, maker, type) match the query come back beside the blocks in `files`, each with its kind (`datasheet` or `file`) and the artifactId to pass to datasheet_facts (`artifact`) or read_artifact.

tools.name: list_wire_predicates
tools.description: List built-in local wire predicates plus custom predicates found in workspace wire snapshots.

tools.name: get_wires
tools.description: Return active local workspace wires connected to a document, or to a typed object. Give exactly one of documentId and iri. A wire may end at an object (a typed object drawn on a whiteboard as a card): such a wire reports sourceIri or targetIri in place of the document id. A wire drawn on a whiteboard reports sceneDocumentId (the board) and sceneElementId (the arrow); asking for a board with direction both also lists the wires drawn on it.

iri.description: The absolute IRI of a typed object, instead of documentId.

tools.name: create_wires
tools.description: Create one or more local semantic wires through the workspace CRDT surface. An end is a document (sourceDocumentId, targetDocumentId, optionally with a block) or a typed object (sourceIri, targetIri), never both. The scene* fields record the whiteboard arrow a wire was drawn from. New endpoints must exist in their graphs/documents; an explicit empty predicate is an error. Self-wires are allowed by the vocabulary.

graphIncarnation.description: Optional expected source workspace lifetime, carried to every child queue admission/effect. Not a target-graph or batch transaction. Discover source_pull.mutationCapabilities.expectedGraphIncarnation version 1 first.

graph_incarnation.description: Alias of graphIncarnation; aliases and any wire-item carrier must agree.

sourceIri.description: The wire starts at this object (an absolute IRI) instead of a document. Needs sceneDocumentId: the board the wire is drawn on.

targetIri.description: The wire ends at this object (an absolute IRI) instead of a document; no target document id then.

sceneGraphId.description: Scene provenance: the graph of the board the wire was drawn on.

sceneDocumentId.description: Scene provenance: the board (whiteboard document) the wire was drawn on.

sceneElementId.description: Scene provenance: the arrow's element id on the board.

sceneSourceElementId.description: Scene provenance: the shape the arrow leaves.

sceneTargetElementId.description: Scene provenance: the shape the arrow reaches.

sceneStableKey.description: Scene provenance: a stable key for the arrow, wb:{boardId}:{elementId}.

tools.name: traverse_wires

tools.name: sparql_query_named
tools.description: Run one of a class's CANONICAL named queries (T2 query face, item 11) — byId(subject), currentHeads({asOf?}), lineageOf(subject), countBy(attr) — derived from the class's declared SHACL shape + MaterializationSignature (never a hand-maintained per-class query). Scoping comes from the class's declared store_target ONLY (class_dispatch), so the partitioned-store silent zero is structurally impossible. Membrane-ed classes (e.g. sophia-memory-core): no 'observer' → the shared commons only; with 'observer' → commons ∪ that observer's membrane (RATIFIED default). currentHeads is the SAME server-authoritative reader emporium_heads uses — one 'current head' semantics everywhere. Returns {graphId, vocab, class, queryName, variables, rows, warnings?} — a query returning zero rows for a shape reason (wrong scope, undeclared attr, missing subject) always says so in 'warnings' or as a structured rejection, never a bare empty result.

class.description: The class name declared by the vocab's contract (e.g. 'MemoryRecord').

params.description: Query-specific arguments: 'subject' (a full subject IRI — byId, lineageOf), 'asOf' (epoch-millis or ISO-8601 datetime — currentHeads; omitted = the live read), 'attr' (a declared predicate CURIE/local-name/URI — countBy).

observer.description: A per-agent membrane. Default = the shared commons (RATIFIED: no observer ⇒ commons only). Ignored, with a warning, on a class with no observer membrane.

tools.name: emporium_query
tools.description: T2 item 11a — the OBJECT query face: 'objects out, not rows'. Runs a conjunctive criteria filter over one class and returns HYDRATED, SHAPED objects (the class-signature-scoped predicate span per matched subject, provenance fields included), never a bindings table. The criteria grammar is DERIVED from the class's own declared shape: legal 'criteria' keys = its declared properties (CURIE, bare local name, or full URI); legal operators are datatype-derived — 'eq' universally, plus 'contains' for strings and 'before'/'after' for dateTime. A malformed criterion (unknown key, illegal operator, unparseable value) is a loud structured rejection naming the class's legal keys/operators — never a silent empty result. Observer semantics (RATIFIED, generalized from recall): no 'observer' ⇒ commons only; 'observer' ⇒ commons ∪ that witness's membrane; 'perspectives'="all" ⇒ every discovered witness membrane merged, each result tagged 'witnessGraph' (merged testimony is never anonymous). Classes under the ratified 'contested' conflict policy (e.g. sophia-memory-core) return CURRENT heads by default, each flagged 'contested' with 'siblingHeads' — routed through the SAME unified head reader 'sparql_query_named'/'emporium_heads' use; 'as_of' walks history instead (rejected for a class with no lineage convention). Returns {graphId, vocab, class, criteria, scope:{graphs, perspectives}, totalMatched, limit, offset, nextCursor?, objects:[{subject, rdfType, predicates, contested?, siblingHeads?, witnessGraph?}], warnings?} as JSON, or {graphId, vocab, class, face:'markdown', markdown} when 'face'='markdown'.

class.description: The class name declared by the vocab's contract (e.g. 'MemoryRecord').

criteria.description: {predicateKey: value | {operator: value}} — conjunctive (AND) this wave. Legal keys = the class's own declared properties; legal operators are datatype-derived ('eq' always; 'contains' for strings; 'before'/'after' for dateTime). Omit or pass {} to match every instance in scope.

observer.description: A per-agent membrane. Default = the shared commons (RATIFIED: no observer ⇒ commons only). Ignored, with a warning, on a class with no observer membrane.

perspectives.description: The ONLY legal value is 'all' — merges every discovered witness membrane (cross-witness merge is an explicit, loudly-named act); each result is then tagged 'witnessGraph'. Omit for the default commons/observer scope.

as_of.description: Epoch-millis integer or ISO-8601 datetime string. Historical heads for a contested class as of this instant; rejected for a class with no ratified lineage/contested convention.

face.description: Default 'json' (the structured outcome). 'markdown'/'md' renders the SAME outcome as curl-friendly Markdown text under a 'markdown' key.

cursor.description: A stable-order page offset (this wave); omit for the first page. Use the previous response's 'nextCursor'.

tools.name: emporium_write
tools.description: T-W item 1 — the MCP write surface over the existing spine (I1 gate, SHACL, minting, journal, contested lineage). 'vocab' names ONE registered vocab; 'records' are flat JSON objects with NO 'subject'/'vocab' field (the client never mints identity — Law 2; use 'clientRef' for correlation). Dispatches on the vocab's resolved write_target: 'sophia-memory-core' (a membrane-ed class) routes through the memory lane — records use the SAME camelCase shape 'remember'/'remember_batch' accept (content/scope/kind/contentOrientation/visibility/status/sourceRefs/…) plus per-record 'supersedes'/'contradicts' (Law 3: change is lineage, passed through to the spine's existing supersession machinery — content-hash identity converges on a byte-identical resubmission, outcome 'converged'). Any OTHER registered vocab routes through the generic lane — records use '{kind: <ClassName>, ...predicate fields, localId|clientRef}' (the existing generic-ingest shape); supersedes/contradicts have no machinery there and are REJECTED loudly (a materialize class's only reappearance is a plain resubmission of the same localId/clientRef — the 'Replace'-strategy upsert already performed by the existing subject-scoped reconcile). Law 1 (witnessed or explicitly commons): for a membrane-ed vocab, an observer-less write WITHOUT 'publish: true' is a loud rejection; with 'observer' (top-level, or per-record 'observerAgentId') and no 'publish', the write lands in the writer's OWN membrane; 'publish: true' forces the shared commons (the given observer, if any, is not used for placement — flagged in 'warnings', never silent). A non-membrane vocab has no observer concept — 'publish'/'observer' are accepted as a no-op, flagged in 'warnings'. Law 5: 'dry_run' runs the SAME structural/SHACL validation preview a real apply would (nothing written) and reports the predicted per-record outcome + any violations. Batches are single-vocab (structural) and ALL-OR-HALT: any SHACL/apply failure marks EVERY record 'halted' and carries the shared 'violations' — never a partial write. Returns {graphId, vocab, dryRun, ok, results:[{subject, outcome:'applied'|'converged'|'halted', flags?}], journalRef?, warnings, violations?}.

graphIncarnation.description: Optional expected graph lifetime; supplied non-dry-run fences require active source authority and reach serialized source admission/effects. Discover source_pull.mutationCapabilities.expectedGraphIncarnation version 1 first; do not infer support from a pack hash.

graph_incarnation.description: Alias of graphIncarnation; both must agree if supplied.

vocab.description: The vocab name (e.g. 'sophia-memory-core', 'emporium-bookmark'). ONE vocab per call — a per-record 'vocab' key is rejected.

records.description: Memory lane (vocab='sophia-memory-core'): the remember/remember_batch camelCase record shape, plus optional 'supersedes'/'contradicts' (a subject IRI) and 'observerAgentId' (or bare 'observer'). Generic lane (any other vocab): {kind: <ClassName>, ...predicate fields, localId|clientRef}. NEVER include 'subject' (Law 2) or 'vocab' (Law 3 — batches are single-vocab) on any record — both are a loud, whole-batch rejection.

dry_run.description: Default false. true = the SAME structural/SHACL validation preview a real apply would run — NOTHING is written; the response's per-record outcome and 'violations' are the predicted verdict.

publish.description: Default false. For a membrane-ed vocab (Law 1): true forces the shared commons (an explicit publication act); false (the default) requires an 'observer' — an observer-less write without publish=true is a loud rejection. No-op (flagged in 'warnings') for a non-membrane vocab.

observer.description: The writer's own membrane (a per-agent witness id). Default for every record that omits its own 'observerAgentId'. No-op (flagged in 'warnings') for a non-membrane vocab.

operationId.description: Stable source invocation identity. Batched records derive stable child identities from it.

tools.name: emporium_retract
tools.description: T-W item 2, Law 4 (retraction is an event, not an erasure) — mints a retraction EVENT on 'subject' (who/when/rationale) direct-on-store, in whichever named graph the subject already lives in (located by a store-wide scan; this tool takes no vocab/class). Heads exclude it: `sweep::current_heads_by_lineage`/`heads_as_of` — and therefore `emporium_heads`, `sparql_query_named`'s 'currentHeads', and `emporium_query`'s contested routing — never return a retracted subject as a current (or, for 'as_of', historical) head again. The generic object faces (`emporium_list`/`emporium_read`/`emporium_query`'s criteria match) hide it too. The log keeps it: NO triple is removed — hard-delete stays a SEPARATE, deferred admin-tier act (the existing HTTP-only `DELETE /emporium/objects/…` route, untouched). Re-retracting an already-retracted subject records an ADDITIONAL event (flagged in 'warnings'), never an error. Returns {graphId, subject, graph, kind, rationale, retractedAt, retractionRef, alreadyRetracted, warnings}.

subject.description: A full subject IRI — an existing minted subject the caller read back from a prior write/query (referencing an existing identity is not minting a new one).

rationale.description: Why this subject is being retracted (Law 4: who/when/rationale) — required, non-empty.

observer.description: The witness recording this retraction (attributed via 'retractedBy') — NOT used to locate the subject.

operationId.description: Stable source operation identity. Reuse the same value for an at-least-once retry.

tools.name: workflow_plan_create
tools.description: Start a new workflow: a document of kind "workflow" whose plan is RDF (Choreograph's graph-plan-v1) in the named graph urn:sophia:wf:<documentId>:draft. Creates the document (the server picks its id; parentId files it in a folder), writes a one-paragraph body saying what it is, seeds the draft with <urn:sophia:wf:<documentId>> a wf:Workflow ; wf:name "<documentId>" ; dcterms:title "<title>" (wf: = http://mnemosyne.dev/workflow#), and returns what workflow_plan_read returns (documentId, workflow, draftGraph, phases, report, authoring). Then build the plan with workflow_plan_compose. These tools never run a plan: the person approves and runs it from the workflow pane.

title.description: What the workflow does, as its person would name it.

parentId.description: Optional folder id to file the document in.

tools.name: workflow_plan_read
tools.description: Read a workflow document's plan (graph-plan-v1, RDF in urn:sophia:wf:<documentId>:draft): title; phases in wf:order, each {id, title, order, steps:[{id, label, agentType, mode, over, consumes, checks, produces, instructions, itemSchema, reads, itemClass?, itemVocab?}]} (itemClass, on a class-bound step: {iri, name, vocab, version, source, label, plural, fields}, or {iri, known:false} for a class this graph lacks) with phases, collections and sources named by id; sources [{id, label, documentId, fromBlock, toBlock, documentTitle (when the document is in this graph), readBy (the steps that read it)}] and destinations [{id, label, kind, receives, documentId}], always present, possibly empty; collections [{id, producedBy, itemClass? {iri, label, plural, known}}], every collection a step produces with the class of its items (a check's items are the class of what it checks); report {conforms, problems:[{focus, message, source}]}, what still keeps the plan from running, judged by SHACL shapes (source "shacl"), by the rules Choreograph's compiler applies (source "structure") by whether each document a source or destination names is in this graph (source "workspace") and by whether each step's itemClass is a type of this graph (source "types"); and authoring.recent, the last 10 wf:CompositionEvents {at, actor, rationale, moves}. Read-only. Refuses a document whose kind is not "workflow".

tools.name: workflow_plan_compose
tools.description: Change a workflow's plan with moves, applied in order as one SPARQL update to urn:sophia:wf:<documentId>:draft and recorded as one wf:CompositionEvent (your rationale and the moves) in urn:sophia:wf:<documentId>:authoring. Returns what workflow_plan_read returns. THE GRAMMAR (graph-plan-v1): a workflow has 1 to 6 phases that run in order; the steps of a phase run in parallel (at most 12 steps in all). A step is one agent with a label, an agentType and its instructions. mode "once" runs it once, with the run input or the whole of each collection it consumes; mode "perItem" runs it once per item of the collection named by over. Every step except a check produces one collection (produces) of items shaped by itemSchema, a JSON Schema of ONE item, or by itemClass (below). A check (checks: a collection) runs once per item of that collection, answers pass or refuse, and produces the items it passed; it needs no itemSchema. A step may read (over, consumes, checks) only collections produced in an EARLIER phase, and each collection has exactly one producer. A collection is just an id: name it by producing it. TYPED ITEMS: instead of itemSchema a step may name a class, itemClass: a type of this graph (define one with propose_domain_ontology; list them with emporium_vocab {graphId}) as "<vocab>:<Class>" (e.g. "workspace:DreamReport") or its IRI. Compose writes wf:itemClass, wf:itemVocab "<vocab>@<version>" (the version is pinned: after the class changes, compose the step again) and the class's derived JSON Schema as wf:itemSchema. Give itemClass or itemSchema, not both. A class this graph does not have is accepted but named in the report (source "types"). Each item a class-bound step hands back is recorded as an instance of its class (workflow_run_record); a check's items keep the class of what it checks. SOURCES AND DESTINATIONS: a source is what a step reads: a document of this graph (documentId), or its blocks from fromBlock through toBlock. A step names the sources it reads with reads, and the run tells it what they are, so its instructions can say "the book" instead of a document id. A destination says where the results go: a margin destination (kind "margin", the only kind) publishes each item of the collection it receives (receives, one some step produces) as a comment on the item's exact quote (in its blockId when known) with its note, in the margin of the document the item names, or of the destination's documentId when it names none; workflow_plan_publish does it. At most 6 sources and 4 destinations; the report also names a source or destination whose document is not in this graph (source "workspace"). MOVES: {op:"set_title", title}; {op:"upsert_phase", id, title, order}; {op:"upsert_step", id, phase, label, agentType, instructions, mode?, over?, consumes?, checks?, produces?, itemSchema? or itemClass?, reads?}; {op:"upsert_source", id, label, documentId, fromBlock?, toBlock?}; {op:"upsert_destination", id, label, kind?, receives, documentId?} (kind defaults to "margin"); each upsert replaces that node wholesale (send every field it should keep); {op:"remove", id}, a step, a destination, a source once no step reads it, or a phase once it holds no steps. Ids: a letter, then up to 63 letters, digits, _ or -. A malformed move (unknown op or field, bad id, document id or block id, a kind other than "margin", missing required field, an id that already names another kind of node) refuses the whole call and writes nothing. An incomplete plan is accepted: read report.problems and keep composing until report.conforms is true. EXAMPLE moves: [{"op":"upsert_source","id":"book","label":"The Interpretation of Dreams, I.C","documentId":"freud-ch1","fromBlock":"block-be1fe535"}, {"op":"upsert_phase","id":"p1","title":"Read","order":1}, {"op":"upsert_step","id":"reader","phase":"p1","label":"the Reader","agentType":"segmenter","instructions":"Cut the book into passages, one per paragraph.","mode":"once","reads":"book","produces":"passages","itemSchema":{"type":"object","required":["text"],"properties":{"text":{"type":"string"}}}}, {"op":"upsert_phase","id":"p2","title":"Check","order":2}, {"op":"upsert_step","id":"censor","phase":"p2","label":"the Censor","agentType":"checker","instructions":"Pass a passage only if it quotes the source exactly.","checks":"passages","produces":"verified"}, {"op":"upsert_destination","id":"margin","label":"The book's margin","receives":"verified","documentId":"freud-ch1"}]. Refuses a document whose kind is not "workflow"; writes only that document's :draft and :authoring graphs.

rationale.description: Why, in a sentence; kept in the authoring trail.

id.description: upsert_phase, upsert_step, upsert_source, upsert_destination, remove: the id of the phase, step, source or destination; it names urn:sophia:wf:<documentId>#<id>.

title.description: set_title: the workflow's title. upsert_phase: the phase's title.

order.description: upsert_phase: when the phase runs; phases run in ascending order, each order once.

phase.description: upsert_step: the id of the phase the step runs in.

label.description: upsert_step: the step's name as the person reads it, e.g. "the Reader". upsert_source, upsert_destination: its name, e.g. "The Interpretation of Dreams, I.C", "The book's margin".

agentType.description: upsert_step: the kind of agent, e.g. "segmenter", "extractor", "quote checker".

instructions.description: upsert_step: what the step's agent is told to do, in full (at most 4000 characters).

mode.description: upsert_step: once (default) runs one agent; perItem runs one agent per item of over. A check is always perItem.

over.description: upsert_step: the collection a perItem step runs over.

consumes.description: upsert_step: collections a once step reads whole.

checks.description: upsert_step: makes the step a check: once per item of this collection it answers pass or refuse, and produces the items it passed. A check needs no itemSchema.

produces.description: upsert_step: the collection the step produces (every step but a check needs one; each collection has one producer).

itemSchema.description: upsert_step: JSON Schema of ONE item the step produces (an object, or its JSON text; at most 4000 characters).

itemClass.description: upsert_step: the class of ONE item the step produces, instead of itemSchema: "<vocab>:<Class>" or the class IRI, a type of this graph. Compose pins its version and derives the item schema from it.

reads.description: upsert_step: the sources the step reads (a source id, or a list of them); the run tells the step what each is, so its instructions can name it ("the book").

documentId.description: upsert_source: the document of this graph the source is (required). upsert_destination: the document whose margin takes the items that name no documentId of their own.

fromBlock.description: upsert_source: the block the source starts at; without it, the document from its start.

toBlock.description: upsert_source: the last block of the source; without it, the document to its end.

kind.description: upsert_destination: where the results go. "margin" (the default, and the only kind): comments in a document's margin.

receives.description: upsert_destination: the collection whose items go there (one some step produces).

tools.name: workflow_plan_publish
tools.description: Publish a finished run's findings as comments in the margin of the documents they name. Reads the run graph urn:sophia:wf:<documentId>:run:<runId> (characters of runId outside A-Za-z0-9_- become _), takes the wf:Items of the collection a margin destination receives (wf:Destination; destination names which, by default the plan's first by id) or, in a plan with no destination, of its last collection (what the first producing step of its last phase produces), in wf:position order, and publishes each item whose JSON names a documentId (or names none, and the destination has a documentId), a non-empty quote and something to say (and, optionally, the blockId that holds the quote): a comment with id wf-<runId>-<n> (n = wf:position + 1) on the exact quote, whose text is the item's note or, when it has none, its other non-empty text fields in the item's own order, each "<key as words>: <value>" (whatDone is "what done"), joined with "; " and cut at 600 characters (an item whose only text is its quote is skipped), anchored as edit_comment anchors (blockId + find; with no blockId, the first block whose text holds the quote), so publishing again updates those comments instead of doubling them. All comments for one document are written in one transaction. For a class-bound collection whose class declares presentation.roles, the item keys named there stand for quote, note, documentId and blockId (a role it does not name keeps its key). A quote that cannot be anchored is reported in notFound, never silently dropped; target documents must be in this graph. Records one wf:Publication in urn:sophia:wf:<documentId>:authoring (with wf:destination when one was used). Returns {collection, destination (when one was used), placed, notFound:[{index, quote, reason}], documents, skipped}. Refuses a document whose kind is not "workflow".

runId.description: The run whose findings to publish (as the workflow pane shows it).

destination.description: Optional: the id of the margin destination whose collection to publish; by default the plan's first by id. A plan with no destination publishes its last collection.

tools.name: workflow_run_record
tools.description: Record a finished workflow run's results in the workflow document's own run graph, urn:sophia:wf:<documentId>:run:<runId> (characters of runId outside A-Za-z0-9_- become _, as workflow_plan_publish reads it). A workflow runner (Sophia Compute) calls it when a run ends, with the run's triples as Turtle: the wf:GraphPlanRun node, its wf:Items, wf:Refusals and wf:StepRuns. Only triples about that run are taken: every subject must be the run graph's IRI itself or <that IRI>#<fragment> (no blank-node subjects); objects may name anything, such as the plan's workflow, steps and collections. The call replaces the run graph's contents with exactly those triples in one transaction, so recording the same run again is idempotent; Turtle that does not parse, or any triple about something else, refuses the whole call and writes nothing. It needs only document-write scope (documents.write.crdt), not RDF admin (rdf.update), so a runner holding a member's token can record its runs; the workflow pane and workflow_plan_publish see the graph at once. TYPED ITEMS: for each wf:Item of a collection whose producing step names a class (wf:itemClass; a check's items take the class of what it checks), the cell maps the item's wf:json onto the class (its keys are the class's field keys; a nested value becomes a child node <item>/<key>, or <item>/<key>/<i> in a list) and checks it against the class's shapes, in the same transaction. An item that fits gains a <Class>, its field triples, wf:itemVocab, wf:producedBy (the being cast for the maker's step: send <run#step-n> wf:castAgent <agent IRI> on each wf:StepRun), wf:checkedBy (the checker's being, for a checked collection) and prov:generatedAtTime (the item's own, else the run's prov:endedAtTime, else the time of recording); one that does not fit is typed wf:Unfit with wf:itemClass and one wf:violation per problem, never dropped. CAST REGISTRATION: each canonical being named by a wf:StepRun's wf:castAgent for a post in this workflow's draft is registered as agt:Agent in urn:sophia:wf:<documentId>:agents, with agt:agentId, rdfs:label from the post, wf:partOfWorkflow and wf:step, in the same transaction. Re-recording updates these annotations without adding duplicate registrations. A per-item wf:sitting "<label>" is an ordinary triple. Returns {graph, triples} (the run graph's IRI and how many distinct triples it now holds) and, when the plan has a class-bound collection, {typed, unfit} counts. Refuses a document whose kind is not "workflow".

runId.description: The run being recorded (as the workflow pane shows it), 1 to 128 characters.

turtle.description: The run's triples as Turtle (at most 16 MiB), starting with @prefix wf: <http://mnemosyne.dev/workflow#> . and any other prefixes it uses. Every subject must be <urn:sophia:wf:<documentId>:run:<runId>> or <urn:sophia:wf:<documentId>:run:<runId>#...>.

tools.name: workflow_run_start
tools.description: Validate a graph-native workflow and submit an async Choreograph run through Garden's local service facade. Returns the run id and monitor actions; can optionally start the local Choreograph service.

tools.name: workflow_run_monitor
tools.description: Poll Choreograph run detail and JSON telemetry events through Garden's local service facade. Pass runId directly, or pass graphId + workflowName to monitor the latest recorded run for that workflow.

tools.name: semantic_search
tools.description: Search the prepared local semantic index for a graph.

tools.name: find
tools.description: Find things in a graph's own RDF data by meaning and by words (Spanish, English and other languages): datasets, code-list concepts, classes and properties, organizations, places, people. Each hit is {iri, label, type, score, says, via?}: a distribution or other part answers as the dataset it belongs to, with `via` naming the part that matched. The response names each hit's named graph with its rights or licence, and `next` says how to read every fact of a hit with sparql_query. Use find for data and entities; use search_documents or semantic_search for documents and notes. Answers only for graphs whose owner enabled it (gardend index --graph <id>).

query.description: What you are looking for, in any language: a name, a description, or a need ("fuel prices at the pump").

types.description: Only these type labels, as hits show them (e.g. "department").

graphs.description: Only entities from these named graphs.

mode.description: fused (default): meaning 0.7 + words 0.3; vector: meaning only; lexical: words only (exact names, codes).

tools.name: memory_semantic_recall
tools.description: Semantic recall over the graph's memory projection: embeds `query` and ranks the CURRENT (non-superseded), active memory records by cosine similarity — not a substring match. Pass `cutoff` (an ISO 8601 / xsd:dateTime instant, e.g. "2026-07-01T00:00:00Z") to recall as-of that point in time; only records with createdAt <= cutoff are candidates. Episode memories (kind=EpisodeMemory) are excluded by default — set includeEpisodes to include them. Pass observer_agent_id (an agent id) to search only that witness's memories; without one only the commons (memories filed with no observer) is searched, never a witness's. Returns provider/model/dimensions metadata plus ranked hits (and observerAgentId when one was named); an empty projection returns hits: [] rather than an error.

cutoff.description: ISO 8601 / xsd:dateTime instant (e.g. 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z) with an explicit offset or Z. Only records with createdAt <= cutoff are candidates.

observer_agent_id.description: The witness (an agent id, agent- and 16 hex digits) whose memories are searched. Absent: the commons.

tools.name: semantic_reason
tools.description: Resolve a virtual semantic relation query over the prepared local semantic scaffold.

tools.name: graph_intuition
tools.description: Compile and optionally execute a unified KG-ULTRA graph intuition request, returning an agent-facing storybook with routes for inspection and acceptance.

tools.name: list_restore_points
tools.description: List local time-travel restore points for a graph, newest first, with cursor pagination.

tools.name: get_restore_point
tools.description: Read the manifest of a single local restore point, including referenced per-document snapshot ids.

tools.name: create_restore_point
tools.description: Capture a new local restore point bundling the workspace state with a fresh snapshot of every document. Optional label is shown in listings.

tools.name: diff_restore_points
tools.description: Compute aggregate document and char-level deltas between a restore point and another (or the live workspace).

tools.name: delete_restore_point
tools.description: Delete a local restore point and its bundled workspace snapshot. Per-document snapshots referenced by other restore points remain.

tools.name: restore_to_restore_point
tools.description: Apply a local restore point: captures an auto-backup, atomically swaps Y.Doc state, rematerializes RDF, verifies, and on any failure rolls back from the auto-backup. Blocks all CRDT writes for the duration. Returns an operationId for status polling. Pass dryRun=true to validate without applying.

tools.name: get_restore_operation
tools.description: Read the current state of a restore operation: phase, progress, backup pointer, error if any.

tools.name: cancel_restore_operation
tools.description: Request cancellation of an in-flight restore. Cooperatively checked between phases; if cancelled mid-restore, the auto-backup is rolled back so the graph returns to its pre-restore state.

tools.name: read_artifact
tools.description: Perceive a stored artifact: image kinds return base64 bytes (the agent's vision model can then see it), text returns decoded text, others return metadata.

strict_utf8.description: Strict text/html or text/plain UTF-8, at most 2 MiB; returns actual current contentHashSha256 and graphIncarnation.

tools.name: create_artifact_text
tools.description: Create a new versioned text/html or text/plain artifact, never overwrite. Exact UTF-8 text up to 2 MiB. Bind operation_id to this request for replay; graph_incarnation is required. Original bytes are authority; workspace content identity is a refresh hint.

tools.name: write_artifact_text
tools.description: Replace exact UTF-8 bytes of a text-owned artifact (2 MiB maximum) only if expected_content_sha256 matches current bytes in graph_incarnation. Retains history and rejects stale writes. Same operation_id/request replays its receipt; changed payload conflicts. Equal content is a no-op.

tools.name: list_artifact_kinds
tools.description: List artifact kinds and their capabilities (perceive/render/derive) from the graph-native kind ontology.

tools.name: list_artifact_revisions
tools.description: List the version history (revisions) of an artifact, newest first.

tools.name: restore_artifact_revision
tools.description: Restore an artifact to a prior revision (checkpoints the current state first, so it is reversible).

tools.name: edit_artifact_image
tools.description: Edit or generate an image artifact from a natural-language instruction via an image model, saving the result as a new revision.

tools.name: source_pull
tools.description: Pull one identity-fenced, complete source bundle for a graph. The bundle includes workspace and document Y.Docs, Meaningful Object current-state and event sources, memory, valuations, retractions, conflicts, receipts, and the source contract registry. Persist the whole bundle and its complete manifest atomically before claiming offline completeness.

graphIncarnation.description: Optional on first pull; required on subsequent pulls to reject a replacement graph.

tools.name: source_push
tools.description: Atomically accept a batch of stable, identity-fenced offline source intents, return durable idempotency receipts, and materialize their effects. Current-state Meaningful Objects use causal base versions and explicit conflicts; event sources use stable event identity; Y.Doc updates merge; lifecycle effects are resumable.

tools.name: source_rebuild
tools.description: Recompute disposable Meaningful Object, memory, valuation, retraction, conflict, and workflow projections from the identity-fenced durable source ledger, reporting source and projection set hashes for rebuild verification.

tools.name: flow_seed_board
tools.description: Seed (or wholly replace) the graph's Mithras Flow board from a Flow board JSON file: materializes the board Y.Doc (resource + scene roots), ensures the 'flow-board' workspace entry with documentKind "flow-board", and flushes the :projection:flow lane. Seeding is a whole-board act: a non-empty board is refused unless replace is true.

json.description: The Flow board file content (Flow JSON, form N or any parseable board).

replace.description: Replace an existing non-empty board (default false: refuse).

tools.name: flow_export_board
tools.description: Export the graph's Mithras Flow board as canonical Flow JSON (form C) with the top-level 'sophia' sidecar key. Without restorePointId the live room is read in one consistency point; with restorePointId that restore point's board bytes are exported and the id travels in the file.

restorePointId.description: Export from this restore point's captured board instead of the live room.

tools.name: whiteboard_create
tools.description: Make a new whiteboard: a document of kind "whiteboard" whose content is a live Excalidraw canvas that people draw on in the app and you draw on with whiteboard_apply. Returns {graphId, documentId, title}; parentId files it in a folder. The board starts empty. Read it with whiteboard_read, change it with whiteboard_apply. A whiteboard is also an ordinary document: search_documents finds it by its title, and read_document returns its outline as markdown.

title.description: The board's name as its person would say it (default "Untitled whiteboard").

parentId.description: Optional folder id to file the document in.

tools.name: whiteboard_read
tools.description: Read a whiteboard as it is right now, including what a person is drawing at this moment (the live room when one is open, else the stored board). format "outline" (default) returns: shapes, each live shape as {id, kind, text, x, y, w, h, color, frame?, group?, link?, linkTitle?, by?} (kind is box, note, ellipse, diamond, text, line, frame, image or freedraw; a note is a box with a fill; x,y is the top-left corner and y grows downward; a shape's bound text is folded into its text; color is a name (yellow, blue, green, red, violet, grey, black) or a hex; by says who last drew it: "person" or the tool caller); arrows, each as {id, from, to, label?, style, fromPoint?, toPoint?} where from and to are the ids of the shapes the arrow is bound to, or null with the end point when it is loose; markdown, the board as an outline (what read_document returns); bounds, the box around everything; elementCount, deletedCount and revision, a token that changes whenever the board does, so you can tell whether anything changed since your last read. format "elements" returns the raw Excalidraw element JSON, live and deleted, for fidelity. Read-only. Refuses a document whose kind is not "whiteboard".

tools.name: whiteboard_apply
tools.description: Draw on a whiteboard with moves, applied in order in ONE transaction on the live board, so anyone with it open sees the result within about a second, with no reload. Returns what whiteboard_read returns, plus created ({ref: elementId} for every shape or arrow the call made) and changed (how many elements were written). You never compute pixels: with neither at nor near an add is placed in free space to the right of everything already there (or at the origin on an empty board); near places it beside a shape and keeps it off the others. THE MOVES: {op:"add", ref?, shape:"box"|"note"|"ellipse"|"diamond"|"text"|"frame", text?, at?:{x,y}, near?:{id|ref, side:"right"|"left"|"above"|"below", gap?}, size?:{w,h}, color?:"yellow"|"blue"|"green"|"red"|"violet"|"grey"|"black"|"#hex"} (text in a box, note, ellipse or diamond becomes its label, centred; a note is a yellow filled box unless you pick a colour; on a box, color is the outline; ref names it for later moves in this call); {op:"connect", ref?, from, to, label?, style?:"solid"|"dashed", head?:"arrow"|"none"} (an arrow glued to both shapes, which follows them when either moves; from and to are shape ids or refs); {op:"update", id, text?, color?, link?} (text replaces the label; link "" removes a link); {op:"move", id, at?|near?|by?:{dx,dy}} (exactly one; the shape's label goes with it and every arrow bound to it is re-routed); {op:"delete", id} (removes the shape, its label and the arrows bound to it); {op:"link", id, documentId? | iri? | url?} (makes the shape open a document of this graph, a typed object's IRI, or an http(s) page when clicked); {op:"group", ids, frame?:"<title>"} (with frame, a titled frame is drawn around them; without, they move together). {op:"card", ref?, documentId? | iri?, at?|near?, size?} (puts a document of this graph, or a typed object by its IRI, on the board as a live card that shows its title and fields and opens it when clicked; the target must exist in this graph, else the call is refused); {op:"wire", arrow, predicate} (promotes an arrow to a stored wire between what it joins, named by predicate, a short name such as supports or an IRI; arrow is an arrow id or a ref from an earlier connect; a predicate that does not make a valid IRI, such as one with spaces, refuses the call and writes nothing). In link, iri must name an object of this graph. Ids are the ids whiteboard_read gives. A malformed move (unknown op or field, unknown id or ref, a colour that is not in the palette, a bad side) refuses the whole call and writes nothing; the error names the move. At most 200 moves. EXAMPLE: [{op:"add",ref:"a",shape:"note",text:"displacement",near:{id:"<condensation id>",side:"below"}},{op:"connect",from:"<dream-work box id>",to:"a",label:"displaces"}]. Read the board first so you move what is there instead of drawing over it. Refuses a document whose kind is not "whiteboard".

ref.description: add, connect: a name for what this move makes, so later moves in this call can use it.

text.description: add, update: the words on the shape.

at.description: add, card: exact position of the top-left corner.

near.description: Place beside an existing shape: {id|ref, side, gap?}. The shape is moved off any other shape it would overlap.

ref.description: A ref from an earlier add in this call.

size.description: add: width and height in pixels; by default sized from the text.

color.description: add, update: yellow, blue, green, red, violet, grey, black or a #hex.

from.description: connect: the shape (id or ref) the arrow leaves.

to.description: connect: the shape (id or ref) the arrow reaches.

head.description: connect: arrowhead at the end (default arrow).

id.description: update, move, delete, link: the shape's id (or a ref).

by.description: move: shift by this many pixels.

link.description: update: a URL or IRI to open; empty removes it.

documentId.description: link, card: a document of this graph.

iri.description: link, card: the IRI of a typed object of this graph.

frame.description: group: draw a frame with this title around them.

arrow.description: wire: the arrow (id or ref) to promote to a wire.

predicate.description: wire: the wire's predicate, a short name without spaces (supports, condensesInto) or an absolute IRI.
